segments.t: Left alone at Mathias's desk, Camille looks for the paternity document on his computer. Instead, she spots an open draft email detailing Mathias's ruthless plot to deceive author Ulrika. Let's listen to this chilling discovery in French first.
Voyons ce formulaire sur son ordinateur.
Attends, qu'est-ce que c'est que ça?
C'est un brouillon d'e-mail ouvert.
J'ai fait des promesses à Ulrika...
Pour qu'elle signe le contrat...
Mais je compte la décourager progressivement...
On peut la remplacer plus tard...
Utiliser la note de frais...
Pour une fondation animale...
Mon Dieu, c'est une trahison totale!
Il a menti à tout le monde.
Camille? Tu as trouvé ce formulaire?
Voici deux verres pour fêter ça!
Oui, tout va très bien, papa.
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Voyons ce formulaire sur son ordinateur.
'Let us look for this form on his computer.' Camille prepares to search for the legal paperwork. Notice how 'let us see' leads directly into the noun meaning 'form'.
Attends, qu'est-ce que c'est que ça?

'Wait, what is this?' Camille is distracted by an unexpected open window on the screen. Notice how the short vowel drops before a vowel sound around 'wait', making the phrase flow smoothly as one unit.
C'est un brouillon d'e-mail ouvert.
'It is an open draft email.' Camille notices an unsent message written by Mathias. The key noun here means 'draft', anchored by its matching French article.
J'ai fait des promesses à Ulrika...
'I made promises to Ulrika...' Camille reads the beginning of her father's private strategy notes. Notice how 'have' leads directly into the noun meaning 'promises'.
Pour qu'elle signe le contrat...
'So that she signs the contract...' Camille discovers how Mathias persuaded the Swedish author. Notice how 'signs' leads directly into the noun meaning 'contract'.
Mais je compte la décourager progressivement...
'But I plan to discourage her gradually...' Camille discovers his plan to push the author aside. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'plan'.
On peut la remplacer plus tard...
'We can replace her later on...' Camille reads that Mathias intends to bring in a new writer. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'can'.
Utiliser la note de frais...

'Use the expense account...' Camille uncovers his plan to charge the company for personal schemes. The verb meaning 'to use' pairs naturally with the noun for 'expense account' in everyday conversation.
Pour une fondation animale...
'For an animal foundation...' Camille reads how Mathias planned to feign charitable support. The key noun here means 'foundation', anchored by its matching French article.
Mon Dieu, c'est une trahison totale!
'My God, this is total betrayal!' Camille realizes that her father betrayed both her and ASK. The adjective meaning 'total' takes its feminine form here to match the noun it describes.
Il a menti à tout le monde.
'He lied to everyone.' Camille sees clearly that Mathias manipulated everyone around him. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'has'.
Camille? Tu as trouvé ce formulaire?
'Camille? Did you find that form?' Mathias returns from the kitchen holding two glasses. The verb meaning 'have' pairs naturally with the noun for 'form' in everyday conversation.
Voici deux verres pour fêter ça!
'Here are two glasses to celebrate this!' Mathias approaches warmly to toast their reunion. Notice how 'to celebrate' leads directly into the noun meaning 'glasses'.
Oui, tout va très bien, papa.

'Yes, everything is fine, dad.' Camille conceals her devastation behind a composed expression. The verb meaning 'goes' pairs naturally with the noun for 'dad' in everyday conversation. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

Horrified by the evidence of her father's treachery, Camille quickly hides her discovery as Mathias returns. When you watch the episode, listen out for the expressions meaning 'let us see' and 'form'. You'll catch them now. See you next time.
